text.name: Production Planning
text.tagline: Order-driven planning of materials, capacity and production scheduling
text.description: Using orders and sales forecasts, bills of materials and work center capacity, the Cyber ERP Production Planning module calculates material and resource requirements for production. Master and detailed plans, production orders and Gantt charts make it possible to adjust and reschedule operations. Recording production output, material consumption, scrap and downtime in connection with inventory, purchasing and maintenance helps compare plans with actual performance.
benefits: Estimation of the materials and resources production needs
Planning based on orders and sales forecasts
Identification of capacity constraints and production bottlenecks
Rescheduling when capacity changes or downtime occurs
Control over material consumption, scrap and production output

text.name: Material Requirements Planning
text.cardText: Calculate material requirements and shortages and raise supply requests to carry out production plans.
text.tagline: Material requirements based on the production plan and stock
text.description: Using the production plan and bills of materials, the Material Requirements Planning system estimates requirements for raw materials and semi-finished goods. Checking stock and netting requirements form the basis for identifying shortages and raising material or purchase requests. Integration with inventory and procurement makes it easier to follow up the materials needed for production plans.
benefits: Material requirements derived from the bill of materials
Stock on hand considered when calculating requirements
Identification of material shortages in plans
Supply requests coordinated with inventory and purchasing

text.name: Operations Planning
text.cardText: Set production plans and work orders, view Gantt charts and reschedule when conditions change.
text.tagline: Scheduling production operations across work centers
text.description: The Operations Planning system schedules production plans based on the sequence of activities and available resources. Planning methods and Gantt charts make it possible to set when and at which work center each job is performed. Recording a baseline and comparing revised plans helps review changes and plan deviations.
benefits: Schedules shown on a Gantt chart
Coordination of operation sequence and capacity
Rescheduling when conditions change
Plans compared against the baseline

text.name: Product Engineering
text.cardText: Maintain bills of materials and manufacturing operations as the basis for planning and resource estimation.
text.tagline: Defining product structure, materials and manufacturing operations
text.description: The Product Engineering system defines the materials and operations required to make a product in the bill of materials and engineering data. Recording product attributes and production resources, and using bill of materials templates, make it easier to prepare product master data. This information is the basis for material requirements calculation and operations planning.
benefits: Integrated product manufacturing data
Clearly defined materials and operations
Use of bill of materials templates
Master data for production planning

text.name: Capacity Planning
text.cardText: Compare workload with work center capacity to identify bottlenecks and available time.
text.tagline: Reviewing work center capacity and production constraints
text.description: The Capacity Planning system reviews work center capacity against production plans. Identifying idle or overloaded work centers and calculating available capacity helps assess whether orders can be accepted. Taking downtime and capacity changes into account also makes it possible to adjust production plans.
benefits: Identification of overloaded work centers
Review of idle production capacity
Support for order acceptance decisions
Plans aligned with capacity changes

text.name: Production Control
text.cardText: Record production output, material consumption, scrap and downtime by work order and work center.
text.tagline: Recording actual performance and tracking production variances
text.description: The Production Control system records production time and quantity, materials consumed, substitute items and scrap. Recording shop-floor personnel, operating parameters and the causes of downtime or reduced capacity makes performance details available. Reports on plan status and material consumption make it possible to review plan execution and the causes of variances.
benefits: Access to actual production figures
Tracking of consumed and substitute materials
Analysis of scrap and downtime
Work order execution compared with the plan

text.name: Product Development (R&D)
text.cardText: Define research objectives and stages and product templates, and issue production orders for prototypes or new products.
text.tagline: Recording research projects and building new products
text.description: The Product Development system records product attributes and variants, as well as the objectives and stages of research projects. New product requests and bill of materials templates prepare the information needed for manufacturing. Issuing production orders and reviewing production output, scrap and downtime make it easier to follow up development activities.
benefits: Research objectives and stages kept on record
Definition of product attributes and variants
Manufacturing templates for new products
Tracking of build results and production output
